plan: My value is $21. In a single-round auction with independent values, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value. Other bidders likely have random values between $0-$49. If I bid too high, I risk paying more than my value. If I bid too low, I might lose. I'll aim to bid close to my value but not exactly at it, creating a buffer that protects potential profit. A bid around $20-$21 seems strategically sound.

My value is $22. In a first-round auction with no prior history, rational bidders will likely bid close to their private value. The optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. If others bid near their values, I want to win only if I can do so without paying more than my value. I'll bid around $20-$21 to create a buffer that allows potential profit while not overpaying.

My optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my value to maximize potential profit. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0-$49, other bidders might bid near their own values. I'll bid strategically to potentially win by underbidding the highest bid while staying close to my true value.
